subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the classification of skill continua used in AQA GCSE PE?
questions.explain: AQA uses the basic–complex, open–closed, self-paced–externally paced and gross–fine continua to classify skills.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a closed skill?
options: It is performed in a stable, predictable environment and is usually self-paced
It is performed in a constantly changing environment affected by opponents
It always uses large muscle groups and big movements
It must always be performed as quickly as possible
questions.explain: Closed skills are done in a predictable, unchanging environment where the performer controls the timing, such as a free throw.

questions.q: A gymnast performs a floor routine in a quiet hall and decides exactly when to begin each move. This skill is best classified as:
questions.explain: The stable environment makes it closed and the performer controlling the start makes it self-paced.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a gross skill?
options: A movement using large muscle groups, such as a rugby tackle
A small, precise movement, such as a dart throw
A skill performed in a constantly changing environment
A skill controlled entirely by the opponent's timing
questions.explain: Gross skills involve large muscle groups and big powerful movements, whereas fine skills use small, precise movements.

questions.q: In goal setting, what does the acronym SMART stand for?
questions.explain: SMART targets are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound.

questions.q: In a SMART target, what does the letter 'T' stand for?
questions.explain: The 'T' means the target is time-bound, so it has a set deadline by which it should be achieved.

questions.q: What is a main purpose of setting SMART targets for a performer?
options: To increase motivation and to improve and measure performance
To guarantee the performer wins every competition
To remove the need for any training
To reduce the amount of feedback a coach must give
questions.explain: SMART targets help optimise motivation and give clear, measurable goals to improve performance.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of a SMART target?
options: I will reduce my 100m sprint time from 14.0s to 13.5s within eight weeks
I want to get much faster at running soon
I will try my best to be a better sprinter
I hope to win more races this year
questions.explain: This target is specific, measurable and time-bound, unlike the vague alternatives.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the stages in the basic information processing model?
questions.explain: The basic model runs input, then decision making, then output, then feedback.

questions.q: In the basic information processing model, which stage involves gathering information from the environment using the senses?
questions.explain: Input is the stage where information is received from the environment through the senses.

questions.q: What happens during the decision-making stage of information processing?
options: The performer selects the most appropriate response from memory
The muscles carry out the chosen movement
Information is received through the senses
The result of the action is reviewed
questions.explain: Decision making is where the performer chooses the best response based on the input received.

questions.q: A netballer sees an opponent move (input) and then chooses to pass to a free teammate. Choosing the pass is an example of which stage?
questions.explain: Selecting which response to make from the available options is the decision-making stage.

questions.q: Which of the following lists four types of guidance used in sport?
questions.explain: The four types of guidance are visual, verbal, manual and mechanical.

questions.q: Which statement best describes manual guidance?
options: The coach physically supports or moves the performer's body
The coach uses equipment such as a harness or float
The coach demonstrates the skill for the performer to copy
The coach explains the skill using spoken instructions
questions.explain: Manual guidance involves physical support from the coach, such as holding a gymnast during a move.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of mechanical guidance?
options: Using a float to support a beginner swimmer
A coach explaining the rules verbally
Watching a video of a professional performer
A coach physically holding a gymnast's waist
questions.explain: Mechanical guidance uses equipment or aids, such as a swimming float or trampolining harness.

questions.q: Which type of feedback comes from within the performer, such as the kinaesthetic feel of a movement?
questions.explain: Intrinsic feedback comes from within the performer through the feel of the movement.

questions.q: According to the inverted U theory, how does performance change as arousal increases?
options: Performance improves up to an optimal point, then declines as arousal increases further
Performance continually improves as arousal increases
Performance continually decreases as arousal increases
Arousal has no effect on performance
questions.explain: The inverted U theory states performance rises with arousal to an optimal point, then falls with over-arousal.

questions.q: According to sports psychology, fine and complex skills are generally performed best at what level of arousal?
options: A very high level of arousal
Arousal makes no difference to them
questions.explain: Fine and complex skills require lower arousal so that precision and control are not lost.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes direct aggression?
options: Aggression that involves physical contact with an opponent
Aggression aimed at an object to gain an advantage
questions.explain: Direct aggression involves physical contact with an opponent, such as a heavy tackle.

questions.q: A frustrated badminton player smashes the shuttlecock as hard as possible to win the point, with no contact with the opponent. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Indirect aggression is channelled through an object rather than physical contact, such as smashing a shuttlecock or ball.

specSource: AQA GCSE Physical Education (8582) specification; Sports Psychology
